title: SeaweedFS: Anonymous ListObjectsV2 bypasses an explicit bucket-policy s3:ListBucket Deny on ACL public-read buckets
summary:
## Summary

SeaweedFS supports two access-control mechanisms on the S3 gateway: bucket ACLs (including the `AllUsers` READ grant that marks a bucket public-read) and bucket policies (IAM-style JSON documents with explicit Allow/Deny statements). AWS S3 semantics, which the project documents itself as following, require that an explicit Deny in a bucket policy overrides any ACL grant. SeaweedFS's own policy engine states the same invariant in code: explicit Deny trumps everything.

This precedence is not enforced for anonymous requests on public-read buckets. The `AuthWithPublicRead` middleware checks the bucket's cached ACL status first and, when the bucket is public-read, dispatches straight to the request handler without ever consulting the bucket policy engine. Object content is still protected because `GetObjectHandler` and `HeadObjectHandler` re-evaluate the bucket policy inside the handler after fetching the entry. `ListObjectsV2Handler` has no such re-evaluation, so an unauthenticated caller can enumerate the full object namespace (key names, sizes, ETags, owners, timestamps) of a public-read bucket whose listing the operator explicitly denied with a bucket policy statement.

The affected pattern is the AWS-recommended way to run a public bucket whose key namespace must stay private: a public-read ACL for content delivery plus an explicit `Deny` on `s3:ListBucket`. On SeaweedFS the Deny is enforced against every authenticated principal and silently ignored for anonymous callers.

## Attacker position and trust boundary

- Starting position: fully unauthenticated network client with TCP access to the S3 gateway port. No credentials, no identity, no bucket membership.
- Deployment: S3 gateway with authentication enabled (static identities or the IAM integration; verified with static `s3.json` identities) and at least one bucket configured with a public-read ACL plus a bucket policy containing an explicit `Deny` on `s3:ListBucket` for principal `"*"`.
- Trust boundary crossed: the explicit administrative Deny that the operator placed on the bucket. An anonymous principal reaches data (object metadata) that every credentialed principal, including the admin identity itself, is denied.

## Source-level call chain

1. Route registration wraps `ListObjectsV2Handler` in `AuthWithPublicRead`:

`weed/s3api/s3api_server.go:1005-1008`

```go
   bucket.Methods(http.MethodGet).HandlerFunc(track(s3a.AuthWithPublicRead(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
       limitedHandler, _ := s3a.cb.Limit(s3a.ListObjectsV2Handler, ACTION_LIST)
       limitedHandler(w, r)
   }, ACTION_LIST), "LIST")).Queries("list-type", "2")
```

2. `AuthWithPublicRead` checks the cached public-read flag and short-circuits to the handler before any policy evaluation happens. The policy engine is only consulted when the ACL check did not already grant access:

`weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_handlers.go:904-949`

```go
   func (s3a *S3ApiServer) AuthWithPublicRead(handler http.HandlerFunc, action Action) http.HandlerFunc {
       return func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
           bucket, object := s3_constants.GetBucketAndObject(r)
           authType := getRequestAuthType(r)
           isAnonymous := authType == authTypeAnonymous
           if isAnonymous {
               // First check ACL-based public access
               isPublic := s3a.isBucketPublicRead(bucket)
               if isPublic {
                   glog.V(3).Infof("AuthWithPublicRead: allowing anonymous access to public-read bucket %s (ACL)", bucket)
                   handler(w, r)
                   return
               }
               // Check bucket policy for anonymous access using the policy engine
               principal := "*" // Anonymous principal
               allowed, evaluated, err := s3a.policyEngine.EvaluatePolicy(bucket, object, string(action), principal, r, nil, nil)
               ...
```
